candidate_relations.reason: Good syndrome is defined as thymoma combined with hypogammaglobulinemia/immunodeficiency. The clinical record confirms type AB thymoma (Masaoka-Koga 2A) plus decreased IgG, decreased B lymphocytes, and inverted CD4:CD8 ratio — all hallmarks of Good syndrome. Naming only the thymoma omits the immunodeficiency component that constitutes the full diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Type AB thymoma is a required component/cause of Good syndrome but does not capture the full diagnostic entity, which additionally requires hypogammaglobulinemia and the associated immunodeficiency syndrome

case_quality_flags: Indirect immunofluorescence and ELISA/immunoblot negative, supporting non-autoimmune mucosal disease in context of immunodeficiency rather than pemphigus/pemphigoid
Oral lichenoid/erosive lesions in Good syndrome are a recognised manifestation; diagnosis rests on the composite of thymoma plus hypogammaglobulinemia
